minutes.headline: Water commissioners sent a reply letter to Hickory Hills and Woodlands residents, refusing road payments and binding lake-level terms.
minutes.summary: The meeting was mostly about the Hickory Hills well pilot study. Commissioners and residents argued over lake levels, Woodlands road damage and a conservation filing. The board also heard a developer ask about water on Howard Street. The preliminary budget discussion was tabled.

public_comment.topic: Urged testing the well, no special agreements or road surcharges for some customers, and monitoring of lake levels.
A speaker rebutted claims about the treatment plant, grant funding for the pilot study, and PFAS scare tactics.
Asked Mr Jeffries whether he was invited and had reviewed earlier meetings.
A speaker clarified the select board backed only the pilot study, not a treatment plant.
Miss Bertram responded to the letter on wetlands rules, discharge volume, pump tests, loggers and studies of wells affecting lakes.
Asked for a small contribution to Woodlands road deterioration from water district trucks.
Asked whether attorneys had answered on a water main, a well or a tank for his Howard Street project.
Mr Rogers said the board should wait for the zoning board decision.
Mr Rogers read the easement language on water rights.

votes.motion: Approve the January 4th 2023 response letter to the Hickory Hills and Woodlands letter

budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner said the pilot study is the first step to apply for grants, and that state revolving fund money is mostly going to PFAS treatment.
Notifying abutters and permitting fees would be an unbudgeted expense outside the engineering contract.
The budget discussion was tabled until a first-step draft is prepared.

decisions.decision: The letter says the district cannot enter legal agreements with the Hickory Hills landowners and will not pay for road upkeep now.

what_happened.line: The Water District voted on a January 4th 2023 reply letter to the Hickory Hills and Woodlands residents; the vote tally was not audible in the recording.
The letter says the district cannot enter legal agreements with the Hickory Hills landowners and will not pay for road upkeep now.
Commissioners and residents discussed the Hickory Hills well pilot study, lake levels, Woodlands road damage and a conservation filing.
A developer asked whether a water main, well or tank could serve a Howard Street project; no resolution was reached.
Discussion of the preliminary 23-24 budget was tabled until a first-step draft is prepared.

why_it_matters: The pilot study is described as the first step toward grant applications, so how the Hickory Hills well proceeds bears on what water customers may later be asked to fund.

Permitting and abutter-notice costs for the conservation filing were described as outside the engineering contract and unbudgeted, a cost that would have to be covered from somewhere in the district's budget.
With the 23-24 budget tabled, no draft figures were in front of the public at this meeting.
